key_insight: Velocity Matching learns continuous-time dynamics without training-time rollouts, avoiding long-horizon objective degeneration and numerical-solver bias.
engineering_relevance: For nonlinear ODE and semi-discretized PDE models, it offers a way to learn accurate dynamics without repeatedly simulating and backpropagating through numerical solvers.
method: Use piecewise-linear trajectory interpolation and stochastic collocation to construct a simulation-free velocity objective.
Approximate velocity population risk to second order in the sampling step.
Link velocity errors to trajectory errors through stability estimates.
evidence_signal: Experiments on nonlinear ODEs and semi-discretized time-dependent PDEs report improved accuracy over trajectory-based objectives; the abstract provides no quantitative gains.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on temporal sampling resolution; the abstract does not establish robustness to noisy or sparsely sampled observations.
paper_title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
